note: Written; validate_items.R --table-sets passes (20/20 items, resp 1-5 exact). Caveats: (a) administered in Italian to Italian primary-school children in Perugia and no Italian wording is published anywhere in the article or its supplements, so the S2 File's English ships in the base fields with language=Italian and empty _translated columns (text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied); (b) the activities were shown as PICTURES, so item_text is the codebook's verbal description of each picture rather than a stem any child read; (c) mapping_basis=paper_order -- the item code IS the S1 workbook column name (data/meloni_2015_disability.py melts the IA*_* columns with no rename and no positional step), so the four blocks are given by the deposit, but the S2 codebook lists the 20 activities as one flat (i)..(xx) list tied to no code, so position 1..5 within a block is inferred from that list order; Step 5b PARTIAL (see verification file); (d) the codebook typo 'read stories form the Bible' is shipped corrected to 'from', as in the sibling frequency table; (e) option_text is populated only at the endpoints ('liked the least' / 'liked the most'), a light expansion of the S2 File's own parenthetical anchors 'a number from 1 (the least) to 5 (the most)'; resp 2-4 carry no label in any source and are left blank rather than padded with their own numbers; (f) the shipped instructions are the task's full verbatim instructions and therefore also name the FREQUENCY card ('1, Never; 3, Once or more a year; 5, Once or more a week'), which belongs to the sibling table meloni_2015_child_ia_frequency, not to this table's 1-5 preference scale -- flagged in the public_note; (g) DATA OBSERVATION (not a text problem): the paper describes preference as an ordering of the five pictures with 'a number from 1 (the least) to 5 (the most)', but ties are pervasive in the deposit -- of the 76 children in the S1 deposit all 76 have a complete block on all four blocks, and only 5/5/6/5 of them (REL/HBODY/SOCIAL/GEN) used all five distinct values; block totals run 3 to 24 (REL 5-21, HBODY 3-24, SOCIAL 7-21, GEN 6-24) rather than a constant 15 -- so resp behaves as a 1-5 liking rating with ties allowed, not a strict rank. [Orchestrator Step 5b re-check, 2026-09-08: the agent reported '74 children ... only 4-5 per block ... totals 6 to 24'. Recomputed directly from the cached S1 deposit (journal.pone.0128876.s001, sheet Dataset_S1, Protocol 200-281): the finding stands -- ties are pervasive and resp is not a strict rank -- but the counts were 76 complete, 5/5/6/5 using all five values, and a total range of 3-24, so the figures above are the corrected ones.]

Written; validate_items.R --table-sets passes (44/44 items, resp 1/1.5/2/2.5/3/3.5/4). Caveats. (1) GENDER OF THE STIMULI: the S2 codebook prints the 11 statements once, as 'Statements (n = 11 x 2 masculine and x 2 feminine): (Masculine) (i) he's bad; ...', so only the MASCULINE set is published. Two of the four targets are female (Maria, blind = SD; Elena, able-bodied = ND), and those blocks were administered in feminine form, which no source publishes. The masculine wording is therefore shipped verbatim for all 44 rows rather than a gender-swapped rendering IRW would have written; see public_note. (2) Administered in Italian to Italian primary-school children in Perugia; neither the article nor S1-S4 contains any Italian wording (S2 re-checked this round: 0 hits for Italian function words), so text_source=translated_substitute with translation_source=study_supplied, language=Italian and empty _translated columns. (3) mapping_basis=paper_order, Step 5b route 8, status PARTIAL. The four target blocks need no inference (the item code IS the S1 column name); what is inferred is statement (i)..(xi) -> DEQ1..DEQ11, and the route cannot separate statements 8 vs 9 (the same two clauses in reversed order, means 2.92/2.89 MD), 1 vs 2 vs 3 (all at the floor) or 5 vs 7. (4) section_prompt names each target using the description the same child protocol gives in the OPEN-ended questionnaire ('Giovanni is in a wheelchair because he cannot walk.', etc.); the codebook states the closed-ended stimuli 'were the same as for the open-ended questionnaire', and without it no shipped row would carry the item's referent. (5) resp 1.5/2.5/3.5 are the codebook's unlabelled intermediate points, so option_text is deliberately blank there, never padded with the number. (6) Typographic apostrophes and quotes in the source were rendered as ASCII; no other character was changed.
